chunks: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

Regarding a man who pronounced li'an (mutual cursing) with his wife while she was pregnant, then claimed her child after she gave birth, asserting it was from him: He said, 'The child is returned to him and he is not lashed, because the li'an has already taken place.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on li'an when the wife is pregnant and the husband claims the child?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that once the formal procedure of li'an is completed, the husband's subsequent claim of paternity does not invalidate the established legal separation, thereby exempting him from the prescribed lashes. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that li'an serves as a definitive proof of non-paternity, allowing for the attribution of the child to the husband while preserving the integrity of the cursing ritual. The decision underscores the finality of the li'an process in resolving disputes of lineage without requiring additional punitive measures.
